problem: The mux count for a two-bit carry-select block is wrong. Two sum bits and the block carry out are each selected, so three 2:1 multiplexers are needed, not two. The same section says 'The carry out of the block is also selected', which contradicts 'two 2:1 multiplexers'.
fix: A plain two-bit block needs two full adders. A carry-select block needs four full adders plus three 2:1 multiplexers: two for the sum bits and one for the carry out.

problem: 'area grows roughly with √n' is technically wrong. Every one of the n sum bits still needs at least one full adder, so area is proportional to n; two ripple adders per block make it roughly double a plain ripple adder. Only the delay falls as √n.
fix: Delay falls to about one block ripple plus a multiplexer tree, while area stays proportional to n — roughly double that of a plain ripple adder when each block holds two copies.

problem: The name 'square-root adder' is used for both carry select (the square-root layout) and carry skip (k = √n). A student may think the two names refer to the same architecture.
fix: Say that the name comes from the √n choice of block size in each case, and that carry select and carry skip are different architectures that both end up with square-root-style delay.
